title: Quarterly synthesis: three-path commitments and commit-window for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define a concise quarterly commitment framework for Hosted API + Model Catalog that maps three operational scenarios (Conservative / Baseline / Accelerate) to specific model onboarding, deprecation, and rollout commitments for Q2 2026. Output: (1) commit window calendar, (2) per-scenario acceptance gates and metrics, (3) cross-team resourcing plan and capacity triggers. Rationale: multiple teams request clearer commitments and predictable windows for model promotions, pruning, and canary schedules. This ticket synthesizes tradeoffs and provides a single source of truth for leadership and ENG/RESEARCH/CONSOLE stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: Published commit-window calendar for Q2 (dates for candidate freeze, canary start, general availability rollout)
Three scenario definitions with explicit throughput/latency/cost thresholds and corresponding model acceptance gates
Owner signoffs from Runtime, Model Onboarding, Console, and Growth (email thread or doc comment)
Clear dependency list and capacity triggers that map to ENG tasks (autoscale, dedicated capacity reservation)
Playbook for rollback and fallback (model variant fallback policy) with runbook links
milestones: 2026-03-12: Draft scenario definitions and candidate criteria created
2026-03-13: Cross-functional review with Runtime & Research — feedback captured
2026-03-18: Finalize commit-window calendar and publish to org Confluence
2026-03-22: Hand off to ENG for capacity reservations and PRs for canary automation
2026-03-31: Leadership signoff and public schedule posted to roadmap page
risks: Insufficient Dedicated capacity allocation could force schedule slip
New model regressions discovered late in canary could increase rollback scope
Misaligned criteria between Research evals and runtime performance targets
Dependencies on third-party model providers (latency/cost) impacting cost targets
